scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for a quality management system where an aerospace organization needs to demonstrate its ability to consistently provide products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. It builds directly upon the baseline requirements of ISO 9001 by adding specific, highly stringent aerospace sector requirements, definitions, and notes.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Quality Management System Standard (Aerospace and Defense Sector)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Quality Management System Certification (Corporate/Organizational Certification). Organizations that satisfy the requirements are eligible to undergo a third-party audit to obtain certification for Aerospace Quality Management Systems (equivalent to AS9100). This certification is universally mandated for any Indian aerospace manufacturer, defense contractor, space components supplier, and maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) facility supplying to organizations like ISRO, DRDO, HAL, and global defense primes.

requirements.detail: The standard incorporates the entire text of ISO 9001:2000 and adds aerospace-specific requirements, definitions, and notes.

Demands a structured configuration management process to ensure that the physical and functional characteristics of aerospace components are fully documented, traceable, and controlled throughout their life cycle.
Specifies rigorous design verification and validation testing, including prototype testing, flight-safety evaluations, and environmental simulation.
Requires a comprehensive, documented first article inspection process to verify that production processes, tooling, and documentation can consistently produce conforming parts per specifications.

Enforces the identification, control, and monitoring of 'Key Characteristics' (dimensions or features of a part that have a significant effect on fit, performance, service life, or manufacturability).
Mandates a formal risk management process for product realization, covering technical, operational, and scheduling risks.

Demands strict flow-down of quality requirements to sub-tier suppliers and maintains end-to-end material traceability from raw ingots (e.g. titanium, aerospace aluminum) to the final installed component.

Imposes strict controls on the identification and segregation of nonconforming materials to prevent their accidental installation on aircraft or spacecraft, including rules for scrap disposal to prevent counterfeit parts.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 16000 : 2004 is the national Indian Standard quality management system specification for the aerospace and defense industries, serving as the identical domestic equivalent of the international AS 9100 standard. Built as an extension of ISO 9001, it adds rigorous sector-specific controls tailored for the high-safety, zero-tolerance environments of aviation and space exploration. The standard enforces strict configuration management, documented First Article Inspections (FAI) to prove tooling capability, continuous monitoring of safety-critical Key Characteristics (KCs), formal risk management in product realization, and absolute end-to-end raw material traceability to prevent counterfeit or nonconforming parts from being installed in flight-critical assemblies.
